description: NaH₅P₂O₆ crystallizes in the monoclinic Cc space group. Na is bonded to six O atoms to form NaO₆ octahedra that share corners with six PHO₃ tetrahedra. There are a spread of Na-O bond distances ranging from 2.45-2.61 Å. There are two inequivalent P sites. In the first P site, P is bonded to one H and three O atoms to form distorted PHO₃ tetrahedra that share corners with three equivalent NaO₆ octahedra. The corner-sharing octahedral tilt angles range from 55-61°. The P-H bond length is 1.40 Å. There is one shorter (1.51 Å) and two longer (1.57 Å) P-O bond lengths. In the second P site, P is bonded to one H and three O atoms to form distorted PHO₃ tetrahedra that share corners with three equivalent NaO₆ octahedra. The corner-sharing octahedral tilt angles range from 50-58°. The P-H bond length is 1.40 Å. There are a spread of P-O bond distances ranging from 1.52-1.60 Å. There are five inequivalent H sites. In the first H site, H is bonded in a single-bond geometry to one P atom. In the second H site, H is bonded in a single-bond geometry to one P atom. In the third H site, H is bonded in a linear geometry to two O atoms. There is one shorter (1.08 Å) and one longer (1.41 Å) H-O bond length. In the fourth H site, H is bonded in a linear geometry to two O atoms. There is one shorter (1.07 Å) and one longer (1.43 Å) H-O bond length. In the fifth H site, H is bonded in a linear geometry to two O atoms. There is one shorter (1.03 Å) and one longer (1.57 Å) H-O bond length. There are six inequivalent O sites. In the first O site, O is bonded in a distorted bent 120 degrees geometry to one Na, one P, and one H atom. In the second O site, O is bonded in a distorted trigonal planar geometry to one Na, one P, and one H atom. In the third O site, O is bonded in a distorted trigonal planar geometry to one Na, one P, and one H atom. In the fourth O site, O is bonded in a distorted trigonal planar geometry to one Na, one P, and one H atom. In the fifth O site, O is bonded in a distorted trigonal planar geometry to one Na, one P, and one H atom. In the sixth O site, O is bonded in a 3-coordinate geometry to one Na, one P, and one H atom.
